Testimonials on-site are suspiciously generic Ñ "Dr. Sarah M., Biomedical Researcher" and "Dr. Jason T., Molecular Biologist" with no verifiable details. Classic placeholder-style copy.
The domain is .org Ñ not inherently bad, but an unusual choice for a for-profit vendor. The original "Apollo Peptide Sciences" used .com, and that domain is now dead. Whether this is a rebrand, a successor, or an unrelated party that picked up a similar name is unclear.
Affiliate program is live (via UpPromote) Ñ not a scam signal on its own, but worth noting in your editorial context since it means reviews tied to that affiliate code may be incentivized.
COA links not publicly posted Ñ their About page claims third-party testing but there's no visible COA library accessible without purchasing.
Scarcity tactics ("Only 2 left __") throughout the storefront Ñ common in dropship-adjacent low-trust stores.
"Definitely Just For Research..." tagline is a winking nod to human use Ñ very common in the space, but it signals a casual compliance posture.

Bottom line for Watchtower:
This vendor has minimal verifiable track record. It's not obviously a scam (it's a functional Shopify store with real product listings and operational details), but it has zero established community reputation. I'd categorize it as unverified / insufficient data Ñ not recommended until COAs can be verified and independent reviews surface. The connection to the now-dead apollopeptidesciences.com is ambiguous and worth flagging to readers.
